newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares jump 2.56 pct on new govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares jump 2.56 pct on new govt hopes.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued their sharp rise on Friday amid new coalition prospects which flared after the resignation of the Islamist-led coalition government late on Wednesday brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,642, up 41 points, or 2.56 percent from Thursday when it leapt 2.3 percent. Trade volume soared further to 27.12 trillion lira from 17.83 trillion on Thursday and 13.86 trillion on Wednesday.

"The market bought on expectations that Mesut Yilmaz would be asked to set up a government. It is obvious that the market will welcome such a development if it becomes true," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
President Suleyman Demirel invited main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Mesut Yilmaz to his residence at 5 p.m. (1400 GMT) amid speculation he would be asked to head a new government.
Yilmaz is one of the favourites to be appointed by Demirel as prime minister-designate following the resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Wednesday.

Yilmaz has earlier said he would exclude the Islamists and seek an alliance with two leftist opposition parties and the other conservative True Path Party which has been the junior partner in the Islamist-led coalition in the past one year.
However Yilmaz, a former prime minister, could have trouble finding the parliamentary majority needed to approve any government he could set up.

"Demirel's invitation to Yilmaz sparked buying in the market, led by state and energy bluechips which caused the index to go up sharply. I expect the index to pierce resistance at the 1,650 level next week," said Serap Arslanalp from Kent securities.
Over the week, the index gained 3.7 percent after diving 5.2 percent last week.

Of the 243 shares traded, rises outnumbered falls by 146 to 42 and 55 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial leapt 2.77 percent to 1,556, IMKB Services soared 3.13 percent to 1,648 and the IMKB Financial firmed 1.66 percent to 1,776.

Actives were led by largely state-owned firms -- oil refiner Tupras, up 3,000 lira at 79,000 and flat steel maker Eregli, up 2,000 lira at 20,500. They were followed by utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 222,500 and Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 217,500. They made up 27 percent of the total turnover.
